Case 02 - Grid Generation & Zonal Statistics

Source: vignettes/case2_grids_zonal_statistics.Rmd
case2_grids_zonal_statistics.Rmd

Partitioning drone flight footprints into operational surveillance grids and extracting zonal summary metrics

1 Objective

Partition the continuous flight mosaic into regular spatial grids (hexagonal or square) with custom parameters, extract zonal summary statistics per cell, identify spatial anomalies using Tukey IQR outlier fences, and export multi-sheet executive spreadsheets.

2 Functions from drones4health

Variable / Target Function Description
Operational Grid d4h_hex_grid() Generates regular hexagonal surveillance partitions using 3 mutually exclusive sizing modes (cell_size, area_m2, or n_cells).
Executive Summary (DF / SF) d4h_executive_summary() Extracts multi-moment statistics and outlier diagnostics, returning both a spatial sf object and a clean tabular data.frame.
Multi-Indicator Extraction d4h_extract_indicators() Simultaneously calculates and extracts multiple biophysical/terrain indicators (ndvi, ndwi, savi, vari, slope, etc.) per region.
Unified Visualization d4h_plot() Unified static and interactive maps with continuous, discrete, or homogeneous baselines.

3 Workflow

3.1 Libraries

We initialize the environment with core geospatial and tabular packages:

library(drones4health)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)

3.2 Spatial Data Preparation

We load the computed environmental indicator rasters (NDVI and NDWI) derived from the drone flight:

# Compute environmental indicators
r_ndvi <- d4h_ndvi(nir = "img/Ohuay_NIR.tif", red = "img/Ohuay_R.tif")
r_ndwi <- d4h_ndwi(green = "img/Ohuay_G.tif", nir = "img/Ohuay_NIR.tif")

3.3 Parametric Grid Generation (3-Way Sizing)

drones4health allows configuring grid cell size using exactly one of three mutually exclusive parameters:

  • cell_size: Distance from side-to-side or diameter in meters (e.g., cell_size = 50).
  • area_m2: Target surface area of each individual grid cell in square meters (e.g., area_m2 = 2500).
  • n_cells: Total number of grid units desired over the surveyed flight footprint (e.g., n_cells = 100).
# Option 1: By diameter/cell_size (50 meters)
grid_hex <- d4h_hex_grid(aoi = r_ndvi, cell_size = 50)

# Option 2: By target cell area (2,500 m2)
grid_area <- d4h_hex_grid(aoi = r_ndvi, area_m2 = 2500)

# Option 3: By target total number of cells (50 cells)
grid_n <- d4h_hex_grid(aoi = r_ndvi, n_cells = 50)

# Inspect generated sf object
head(grid_hex)

3.4 Pipe-Friendly Zonal Statistical Extraction & Summaries

The generated grid directly feeds into d4h_executive_summary(), which automatically detects the grid and returns a complete sf object:


grid_summary_ndvi <- d4h_executive_summary(
  raster_in = r_ndvi,
  grid      = grid_hex,
  out_xlsx  = "salidas/Executive_Summary_Case02_Grids.xlsx"
)

# Returns an sf data frame ready for spatial analysis and plotting
head(grid_summary_ndvi)

3.5 Multi-Indicator Extraction (d4h_extract_indicators)

The d4h_extract_indicators() function provides a unified interface to compute and extract multiple environmental indicators simultaneously across the flight scene:

# Extract NDVI and NDWI in a single call
indicators_sf <- grid_hex |>
  d4h_extract_indicators(
    bands = c("ndvi", "ndwi"),
    nir   = "img/Ohuay_NIR.tif",
    red   = "img/Ohuay_R.tif",
    green = "img/Ohuay_G.tif",
    stat  = "mean"
  )

head(indicators_sf)

3.6 Spatial Grid Executive Reporting & Excel Export

We execute a comprehensive statistical report evaluating descriptive moments (mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, median, IQR), micro-environmental composition (pct_vegetation, pct_bare_soil), and surveillance priorities per grid unit, exporting directly to Excel:

grid_exec_summary <- d4h_executive_summary(
  raster_in   = r_ndvi,
  by          = "grid",
  cell_size   = 50,
  square      = FALSE,
  out_xlsx    = "salidas/Executive_Summary_Case02_Grids.xlsx",
  digits      = 3
)

# Inspect data frame
head(grid_exec_summary$df[, c("grid_id", "area_m2", "pct_vegetation", "pct_bare_soil", "NDVI_mean", "NDVI_sd", "NDVI_median", "dominant_class", "surveillance_priority")], 5)

3.6 Cartographic Visualization & Interactive Grid Mapping

We visualize the operational grid units using the unified d4h_plot() function, switching between static and interactive modes:

# 1. Publication-quality ggplot2 mapping of zonal indicators (interactive = FALSE)
p_grid <- d4h_plot(
  x           = grid_summary_ndvi,
  interactive = FALSE,
  palette     = "viridis",
  title       = "Zonal Surveillance Grid (50m Hexagons)"
)
print(p_grid)

# 2. Interactive web map exploration via mapview (interactive = TRUE)
m_grid <- d4h_plot(
  x           = grid_summary_ndvi,
  interactive = TRUE,
  palette     = "viridis",
  title       = "Zonal Surveillance Grid (50m Hexagons)"
)
m_grid

4 Results & Executive Reporting

4.1 Zonal Grid Executive Summary

The grid-level executive summary evaluates every operational surveillance cell independently, computing descriptive statistical moments (mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, median, IQR), detecting spatial Tukey anomalies per cell, and extracting granular percentage composition across environmental strata:

# Execute zonal grid executive summary per 50m hexagonal cell
grid_exec_summary <- d4h_executive_summary(
  raster_in   = r_ndvi,
  by          = "grid",
  cell_size   = 50,
  square      = FALSE,
  out_xlsx    = "salidas/Executive_Summary_Case02_Grids.xlsx",
  sample_size = 1000000,
  digits      = 3
)

# Preview first grid cells
head(grid_exec_summary, 5)

4.2 Excel Export Structure & Sheet Previews

The workbook exported to salidas/Executive_Summary_Case02_Grids.xlsx contains 2 dedicated sheets:

  1. Grid_Summary: Granular zonal record for every hexagonal cell with descriptive moments, percentage cover composition (NDVI_pct_water_substrate, NDVI_pct_bare_soil, NDVI_pct_dense_vegetation), and Tukey anomaly percentages.
  2. Global_Grid_Summary: Cross-grid aggregated metrics summarizing inter-cell variability across the operational landscape.
